chunks: And Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār asked Abā Ibrāhīm عليه السلام, and he said:
Should one give to a weak person from other than the people of wilayah? He عليه السلام said: "Yes, and the people of wilayah are more beloved to me."

key_terms.أَبَا إِبْرَاهِيمَ: Imam Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar al-Kāẓim عليه السلام.
key_terms.أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ: More beloved to me; indicating preference.
key_terms.أَهْلِ الْوَلَايَةِ: Those affiliated with and loyal to the wilayah of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام.
key_terms.إِسْحَاقُ بْنُ عَمَّارٍ: A narrator who asks the Imam عليه السلام about the ruling.
key_terms.ضَعِيفًا: A weak or vulnerable person, here meaning someone eligible due to weakness or need.

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to give expiation or support to a needy person who is not from the people of wilayah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that it is permissible to give such support to a weak person even if he is not among the people of wilayah. At the same time, it states the preference and greater love for the people of wilayah.
